title: Trace bridge: OTEL-compatible span layer for legacy clients
creator: Priya Menon
description:
Problem: We have several internal and customer services using the Redwood legacy tracing headers (X-Redwood-Trace, X-Redwood-Baggage) and a set of older SDKs that don't emit OpenTelemetry (OTEL) spans. As customers adopt community tooling and we standardize observability, we need a drop-in bridge that allows legacy callers to participate in OTEL-based traces without ripping out client code.

Goal: Implement an OTEL-compatible "trace bridge" layer in the Redwood SDK and edge middleware that:
- Accepts legacy headers and converts them to OTEL SpanContext and baggage.
- Emits spans using the runtime's OTEL pipeline so all traces show up in the same distributed view.
- Preserves per-request sampling decisions and supports overriding via policy (per-route opt-in/opt-out).
- Is low-overhead (<1ms p50 on request path) and feature-gated for gradual rollout.

Scope:
- SDK adapters (Node/Python/Go): parse legacy headers, create OTEL span context, attach to request context, and ensure KV cache and batching flows are unchanged.
- Edge middleware: detect legacy headers at the proxy (and in HTTP/gRPC ingress middleware), translate, and forward standardized trace headers to upstream services.
- Backwards compatibility: if incoming request already has OTEL-format traceparent/tracestate, prefer that; otherwise synthesize from legacy header.
- Baggage handling: map legacy baggage keys to OTEL baggage, dedupe repeated keys, enforce per-header size limits (4KB) and redact values matching PII patterns.
- Metrics/telemetry: emit tracing_bridge.latency_ms, tracing_bridge.error_count, tracing_bridge.trace_mismatch_count.
- Tests: unit tests for header parsing, fuzz tests for malformed headers, integration e2e across gateway -> runtime -> console traces.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- We will not mutate original legacy headers when forwarding; bridge will emit canonical OTEL headers in addition to legacy headers only when feature flag is enabled. This minimizes risk for downstream systems that rely on legacy values.
- Sampling: default behavior is to honor an explicit legacy-sampling flag if present; otherwise, use runtime sampling rules. We will provide a per-route override in the console controlled by a rollout flag to avoid widespread sampling configuration changes.
- Performance: to avoid allocations on hot path, parsing will use a streaming parser and object pooling for span contexts in Node and Go SDKs.
- Security: header size limits and redaction rules are mandatory to prevent header-injection and accidental PII capture. Security review required before GA.

Acceptance criteria:
- SDKs (Node/Python/Go) have adapters that successfully convert common legacy traces into OTEL spans in unit tests.
- Edge middleware can perform translation with median added latency < 1ms under 95th percentile of production-like load.
- Metrics emitted and accessible in Console dashboards. Dashboard snapshot URL included in comments.
- Feature-flag rollout path exists: off by default, can enable per-team, then org-wide.
- Security review completed and remediation items closed.

Out-of-scope for initial patch:
- Automatic retrospective conversion of historic traces.
- Deep integration with third-party tracing backends beyond the runtime pipeline.

Risks:
- Mis-translation causing trace fragmentation (we will track trace_mismatch_count and create alerts at >0.5% of traces).
- Performance regressions in hot paths; mitigation: benchmarking harness and perf regression CI job.
notes: Keep PRs small and modular: (1) header parsing libraries, (2) SDK adapters, (3) edge middleware, (4) dashboards + rollout. Coordinate with Platform and Security for the rollout plan.
comments: 2025-02-14 Priya M: Created ticket and uploaded initial design doc to Confluence. Suggested starting with Node SDK adapter because majority of incoming legacy traffic originates from web clients.
2025-02-17 Liam O'C: Design review done. Decided to prefer incoming traceparent when present. Raised concern about baggage size — added hard limits and redaction.
2025-02-20 Eng Spike: Implemented prototype parser in platform/common/trace. Microbenchmark shows p50 ~0.45ms, p95 ~1.6ms. Need to optimize p95 for heavy payloads.
2025-02-22 Security review kickoff: Security requested additional test cases for header fuzzing and PII patterns. Marked security_review_required = true.

2025-02-25 QA: End-to-end smoke test between edge -> node-sdk -> runtime shows spans correlated in Console for canonical scenarios. Found an edge-case where duplicate baggage keys caused overwrites; added dedupe logic (PR linked).
2025-02-28 Liam O'C: Preparing rollout doc and console toggle. Targeting canary on internal services next week. Added dependency on ENG-8123 for proxy propagation changes.
